canonical_definition: Compositional Reasoning refers to the ability of AI systems to decompose complex tasks into interdependent sub-components or primitives (e.g., functions, skills, concepts) and dynamically recombine or sequence these elements to solve novel algorithmic, planning, or perception-based problems. This construct encompasses function composition (building complex procedures from simpler learned operations), multi-hop reasoning across sub-steps, and cross-domain generalization (e.g., language-to-image alignment, robotic planning), though some sources caution that strong performance on compositionality benchmarks does not necessarily imply robust semantic understanding of the underlying components. Key applications include algorithm learning, closed-loop skill execution, and vision-language reasoning, with operationalizations varying in emphasis on hierarchical decomposition versus inferential combination of primitives.
